overview: This file documents the August 1941 revision of the Japanese colonial Government-General of Taiwan’s regulations governing the entry, residence, and departure of aliens. American Vice Consul Glen Bruner reports from Taihoku that the revised rules, promulgated as Government-General Ordinance No. 153, continued to exempt foreign consular officers, their families, and their employees. The bundle consists of Bruner’s covering despatch to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, an English translation of the notification from Taiwanese colonial official Teruo Hachiya, and Bruner’s formal acknowledgment and thanks.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Bruner to Grew concerning revised alien-control regulations
subfiles.from: Glen Bruner, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Bruner reports that Taiwan’s revised alien-control ordinance does not apply to foreign consular personnel, their families, or their employees.
subfiles.summary: Bruner refers to his despatch of August 22 concerning the Government-General of Taiwan’s August 21 revision of the rules controlling aliens’ entry, sojourn, and departure. He reports receiving a Japanese-language communication confirming that foreign consular staffs, their families, and employees remain exempt. He encloses a translation of that communication and a copy of his reply.

subfiles.title: Translation of Government-General notification on Ordinance No. 153
subfiles.from: Teruo Hachiya, Chief of the Department of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: The Government-General formally notifies the American Consul of the revised alien-control ordinance and confirms the continuing consular exemption.
subfiles.summary: Hachiya states that Government-General Ordinance No. 50 of 1939 was revised on August 21 through the promulgation of Ordinance No. 153 in the Official Gazette. The revised ordinance took effect on the same date. He adds that its provisions, as previously, do not apply to foreign consular staff members, their families, or their employees.

subfiles.title: Bruner’s acknowledgment to Teruo Hachiya
subfiles.to: Teruo Hachiya, Chief of the Department of Foreign Affairs, Government-General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Bruner acknowledges the colonial government’s notification and expresses thanks for confirming the exemption of consular personnel.
subfiles.summary: Bruner acknowledges Hachiya’s communication of August 25, identified as Gai Ryo No. 1,764. He restates that the revised ordinance concerns the entry, sojourn, and departure of aliens and that consular staff, families, and employees remain exempt in accordance with precedent. He closes with formal thanks and assurances of esteem.

interest: The file provides a compact record of how Japan’s colonial administration in Taiwan communicated wartime controls to foreign consulates while preserving diplomatic exemptions. Its combination of covering despatch, translated colonial notification, and formal acknowledgment reveals the complete bureaucratic exchange and the language of consular privilege. Dating from only a few months before the Pacific War, it is especially useful for studying the tightening regulation of foreign mobility, American diplomatic activity in Japanese-ruled Taiwan, and the routine operation of colonial foreign-affairs offices.
